First and second person pronouns in P function take accusative -na. S and A forms are the same for the singular 2nd person pronoun, so it has an accusative alignment. Non-singular 2nd person pronouns have different forms for S and A, and have therefore a tripartite alignment.

Ilongot has ergative-absolutive alignment (Philippine focus system). NOM marker ma marks absolutive NPs (patient of transitive + S of intransitive). Liao (2008:3) ex.(4): kinan ni Madiya ma manok = ate GEN.Maria NOM.chicken ("Maria ate the chicken"). ma is overt ABS marker.

GEN pronoun =ko (1sg agent) vs NOM =/(C)ak (1sg S/O). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1 and §4.2.2: NOM pronoun functions as S of intransitive (ex.14), agent of dyadic intransitive (ex.15), AND theme/patient of transitive (ex.16). GEN =ko marks transitive agent. Ergative alignment on 1sg.
GEN pronoun =mo (2sg agent) vs NOM =ka (2sg S/O). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1 and §4.2.2. Same pattern as 1sg. Ergative alignment on 2sg.

GEN pronoun =to/=tu (3sg agent) vs no NOM 3sg form (zero/absent). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1: 3sg NOM is "---" (no form). Ex.(16): kadɨvaan=tu=(v)ak (accompany=GEN.3SG=NOM.1SG) "She will accompany me" — 3sg agent uses GEN. Ergative alignment present on 3sg (agent marked by GEN).

Full NP: ni (GEN, agent marker) vs ma (NOM, patient/S marker). Liao (2008:3) ex.(4): kinan ni Madiya ma manok noy mase (ate GEN.Maria NOM.chicken last.night) "Maria ate the chicken last night." Overt ergative-absolutive alignment on full NPs.

ERG=GEN: The ergative/agent marker IS the genitive marker in Ilongot. Liao (2008:4) §4.2.1: "the genitive pronoun in Ilongot is used as a nominal modifier AND as the agent of a transitive clause." Resolved from '?' to 1 by structural inference. Ergative 'noh' is a general nominal case clitic (Mang 2006:16) with no person-conditioned split in flagging; the only person sensitivity in the language is in verbal indexation (Mang 2006:20), which GB409 flagging features do not measure. 3rd-person referents (nouns) canonically take 'noh' (ex.6 Ui noh) and 1st/2nd pronouns take 'noh', so 3rd-person pronouns are inferred to do likewise -> erg-abs, not tripartite. NOTE: no free 3sg pronoun token with 'noh' is attested in the grammar; revert to '?' if strict attestation is required.

CORRECTED 1 -> 0. The singular free pronouns are NOT cleanly ergative-absolutive. The regular paradigm (Oates 1988:89-90, Table 4.1) is nominative-accusative: bare NOM serves S and A (1sg ngathu), a distinct ACC serves P (1sg nga-nha). Ergative -ngku then OPTIONALLY marks A (ex.4.85 ngathu-ngku '1sg.ERG'). Combining these, A=ERG(-ngku), S=bare NOM, P=ACC(-nha) are three distinct forms; Oates 1988:100 (Table 4.2) explicitly frames this as an 'ergative-accusative' system overlapping with nominative-accusative. Since S != P (S bare, P accusative), there is no ergative ALIGNMENT (which requires S=P): the pattern is tripartite (or nom-acc), not ergative. Per the tripartite rule (tripartite S/A/P -> 0), coding 0.
